sources.entry: Clementine - Clementine is a modern music player and library organizer for Windows, Linux and macOS.

summary.one_liner: Clementine is a music player and library organizer for Windows, Linux and macOS, and this README mainly covers contribution guidelines, source build steps and formatting rules.
summary.what_it_does: The README is short and mostly developer-facing. It describes Clementine as a modern music player and library organizer for Windows, Linux and macOS, and links to the latest release and pre-release builds. It gives guidance for opening feature requests and bug reports, including checking for duplicates and including OS and version details. It includes build steps for compiling from source with git, cmake, make and sudo make install, and points to the Wiki for dependencies. It also explains that C++ code under src/ is checked with clang-format 23.1.0 in CI, with a dist/format.py script to reformat changed files, and describes how Release-note commit trailers drive weekly numbered releases.
use_cases: Playing and organizing a local music library
Building Clementine from source on Linux
Reporting bugs or requesting features for Clementine
Contributing C++ code with clang-format compliance
Installing the latest Clementine release or pre-release
notable: Cross-platform desktop music player for Windows, Linux and macOS
Weekly numbered releases driven by Release-note commit trailers
CI-enforced clang-format style for src/ with a provided format script
Claude Code formatting hook configured in .claude/settings.json
caveats: README gives only brief build instructions and defers dependency details to the Wiki
